newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals mostly down following NY.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals mostly down following NY.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures, except for palladium, ended the shortened first business day of the year lower across the board on Monday, after spot gold dipped to a three-year low in overseas markets on Friday, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from seven to 12 yen per gram lower, with the most-active benchmark December contract ending down 11 yen at 1,343 yen.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $361.10/60 per ounce at 0242 GMT, against $360.75/361.25 in New York on Friday.
Traders said sentiment in spot gold remained bearish with no bottom in sight, as the gold market has been weighed down, mainly by firm U.S. financial markets and a stronger dollar.

"I have no idea how far gold will dip, as firm U.S. financial markets are reducing the attractiveness of gold. The market lacks any incentive to push up gold at this stage," a trading house trader said.
In the gold futures markets, individual investors who were buying at the opening on the back of the yen's further weakness slackened off later, while trade house selling gathered force.
Traders added India's move to ease gold import restrictions effective from January, would not be sufficient to push up gold.

Palladium futures bucked the trend to end the day firmer across the board, buoyed by firmer bullion prices, but profit-taking capped gains. Palladium futures ranged from four yen to nine yen per gram higher. Most-active benchmark December was four yen up at 438 yen. Benchmark December silver was down 1.9 yen per 10 grams at 178.7 yen. Benchmark December platinum was down seven yen at 1,358 yen.
